title: pinning-resolution-timeline-and-routing-heuristics-wip
content:
Purpose:
This is a working note exploring a concrete operational model for how the control plane should resolve model version pins against routing policies in multi-region deployments. Focus areas: deterministic resolution order, short-circuit fallbacks for partial compatibility, TTLs on pins, and how to express and score compatibility in a simple matrix that control plane can evaluate cheaply at request-time or when making routing decisions offline.

Background / problem statement:
- Customers can pin routes to a model version (e.g., model: 'rw-gpt-13b@v2.4') for stability.
- At the same time routing policies (latency-first, cost-first, region-prefer) want to pick an instance that matches policy, which might mean picking a compatible variant (quantized, fp16, distilled) rather than exact binary match.
- When capacity constraints or regional outages occur, we need deterministic, auditable behavior: which variant is picked, who made the decision (control plane autopilot vs. customer override), and how long that decision holds.

High-level constraints:
- Pins are a stronger signal than a policy but not absolute: customers expect stability but also expect graceful serving if exact pinned version is unavailable (depending on their pin strictness).
- Control plane must be able to score and pick an alternative quickly without contacting model build infra or waiting on long checks.
- Actions must be reversible and observable; state changes should produce events for Console/Logs/Tracing.

Key concepts / vocabulary:
- pin: the record (route -> model:version, pin_mode). pin_mode ∈ {strict, allow-compatible, allow-any} (strings to appear in UI).
- variant: a runtime-compatible build of a model version (e.g., v2.4-fp16-q4_0, v2.4-int8, v2.4-compat-distil).
- compatibility score: numeric stringified bucket (HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW) produced by registry scoring heuristic.
- resolution: the process by which control plane maps route -> variant (or errors).
- pin_ttl: optional time-limited override created by an automated fallback (e.g., 15m) to avoid flip-flopping.

Proposed resolution timeline (ordered steps):
1) Local cache check (fast): check route local cache on serving host for an active pin -> variant mapping, verify TTL not expired. If valid, route to cached variant. (Rationale: low-latency path, avoid control-plane round-trip on hot routes.)
2) Exact pin lookup: consult registry: does requested model@version exist in region and have a healthy pool? If yes, route to exact matching variant (prefer same quant/precision if pin_mode==strict).
3) Compatibility-ladder fallback: if exact not available and pin_mode != strict, consult compatibility matrix to find highest-scoring variant available in region: prefer same version different build (e.g., fp16->int8 fallback), then compatible newer/older patch versions with HIGH score.
4) Cross-region preference: if no compatible variant in region and routing policy allows cross-region, evaluate remote-region candidates using same compatibility ladder + added latency penalty to score.
5) Cost-tier fallback: if still absent and routing policy permits, pick a lower-cost variant (distilled) that meets the minimum score threshold.
6) Canary or degrade: if a best-effort candidate is chosen, the control plane may attach request-time headers and create a short pin_ttl (e.g., 10–60 minutes) to keep routing stable while we monitor quality signals (latency / hallucination metrics).
7) Failure: if no candidate passes minimum compatibility threshold or customer pin_mode==strict -> return route-level error and send event to Console/alerting.

Compatibility scoring matrix (example heuristic) -- simple buckets for speed:
- EXACT_BUILD: HIGH
- SAME_VERSION_DIFF_BUILD: HIGH (if tests pass in registry scoring)
- PATCH_COMPAT(semver minor/patch diff within allowed window): MEDIUM
- MAJOR_VERSION_DIFF: LOW
- DISTILLED/DOWNSTREAM_MODEL: LOW
- UNTESTED_BINCOMPAT: REJECT

Rules to keep evaluation cheap:
- Precompute per-region availability + variant health and cache in control plane lightweight store (TTL 30s).
- Compatibility scores precomputed at model onboarding time and updated on variant builds / quantize runs. For dynamic signals (perf regressions), we attach a health penalty to scores but keep basic bucket.

Pin modes and examples (for UI and JSON wire format):
- strict -> { "pin_mode": "strict", "fallback_ttl": 0 }  // prefer exact, fail fast
- allow-compatible -> { "pin_mode": "allow-compatible", "fallback_ttl": 900 } // 15m autopin when fallback used
- allow-any -> { "pin_mode": "allow-any", "fallback_ttl": 3600 } // give control plane freedom for hour
Note: UI will show a banner when autopin fallback is active with option to "accept and persist" or "revert to strict".

Caching, invalidation, and TTLs:
- Route-local cache (on serving host): store (route,id) -> variant mapping + pin_ttl. Key eviction when TTL expires or when registry publishes invalidation event.
- Control plane cache: stores availability map per region for 30s. When build infra publishes a new variant or decommissions one, we publish invalidation events to control plane cache and to serving hosts.
- Fallback autopin_ttl: short-lived (10–60m) to stabilize routing after a transient failure, but short enough to allow quick recovery when exact model returns.

Observability signals to emit whenever resolution deviates from exact pin:
- resolution_event: {route, requested_model@version, resolved_variant, pin_mode, reason, scorer_version}
- metrics: fallback_rate_per_route, avg_resolution_latency_ms, pin_conflicts, cross_region_routing_rate
- trace tag on requests indicating resolution path (CACHE | REGISTRY_EXACT | COMPAT_FALLBACK | CROSS_REGION | FAIL)

Operational playbook (quick):
- If fallback_rate spikes (>1% of traffic) for a route pinned strict -> page SRE + account owner.
- If compatibility fallback lasting > 6 hours -> create incident to evaluate model build regression or capacity shortage.
- If repeated cross-region fallbacks for a geo -> capacity expansion for that region (automated ticket creation).

Edge cases and discussion notes (unresolved):
- Multi-tenant pools where variants share disks: should we prefer variants with same disk slice to reduce cache warming cost? (tradeoff: may bias routing to certain hosts).
- What is minimal compatibility metadata we require at onboarding such that control plane scoring doesn't rely on heavy tests? (proposal: require semantic compatibility tag + binary-compat flag, optional perf-signature).
- How do we handle pinned chains (route A pins to model X, but routing policy for a dependent route expects a different version)? Need transitive pin resolution rules.
- Rollout interactions: if a new patch version is rolled out progressively, should pins pick up new patch automatically if score==HIGH? Recommendation: allow-compatible picks patches, strict doesn't. Provide explicit "auto-upgrade-patch=true" flag on pin to let customers opt-in.

Open action items:
- [ ] Draft light-weight compatibility metadata schema (owner: Marco)
- [ ] Implement control-plane cache invalidation event schema and publish draft to messaging infra (owner: Leah)
- [ ] Add resolution_event proto to tracing pipeline, with sampling guidance (owner: Sree)
- [ ] UX mock of banner for autopin fallbacks and accept/persist flow (owner: product-console)

Notes for implementation prototype (server-side):
- Keep scoring deterministic: sort candidates by (compatibility_bucket, -health_penalty, policy_penalty, -region_preference_score) then pick first.
- policy_penalty: numeric penalty for deviating from route policy (e.g., cross-region adds +100ms-equivalent penalty).
- health_penalty: derived from 0–100 based on recent error rate and latency deviation; cap to keep buckets stable.
- Persist autopin decisions in a lightweight store with event stream so console can show who/what made the decision.

Appendix: quick ASCII example
Route: /customer/acme/chat -> pinned to rw-gpt-13b@v2.4 allow-compatible
Available variants (region us-west):
- v2.4-fp16 (healthy) -> HIGH
- v2.4-q4_0 (cold cache) -> HIGH (-10 health penalty)
- v2.3-fp16 (warm, slightly lower perf) -> MEDIUM

Resolution run: local cache miss -> exact v2.4 exists but pool saturated -> v2.4-fp16 selected. If pool unhealthy or drained, fallback to v2.4-q4_0 with autopin_ttl=900s and emit resolution_event reason=POOL_SATURATION.

Unresolved UX question: should customers be able to opt out of autopin_ttl creation entirely? (I think yes, via pin_mode=strict or an additional flag).

End of note.

-- Aisha
